etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Recorded in English since c. 1385, as Middle English clamour, from Old French clamor (modern clameur), from Latin clāmor (“a shout, cry”), from clāmō (“cry out, complain”).
The verb sense "to silence" may have a distinct (unknown) etymology.
senses: A great outcry or vociferation; loud and continued shouting or exclamation.
